utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I'm sorry that we were delayed a few minutes coming in; I apologise for that. It is the case that Judge Thelin has been unable to be here. He expects certainly to be able to sit tomorrow. So we will continue sitting under the Rule. Sir, if I may remind you of the affirmation which you made which still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a few matters of clarification which I would like to start with you in relation to the evidence which you gave in response to my questions of last week. The first issue was raised at page 5688 of the transcript. It is the 19th of October of 2007 and in order to refresh your memory, Mr. Bezruchenko, I will read to you the question again. The question was as followings: "So if I understand your response correctly, Mr. Bezruchenko, your suggestion is that yes, this doctrine, military doctrine of operational control applies or can apply to a civilian structure and it does apply in your view to the situation of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that a correct summary." Do you recall my question, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir, but I would say at this point that I also describe the Ministry of Interior not necessarily as a civilian structure but as a law enforcement organisation adaptable to reacting to war situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in response to the question that I had put to you, and I'm grateful for this specification, you had said this: "I'm specifically referring to the forces or, rather, units of the special police of the Ministry of Interior. I don't know to which extent they could be described as civilian structure." And perhaps you have clarified somewhat your answer to me of last week, but I would like to clarify with you whether it is your evidence that the entire Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia was at the time subject to this doctrine of operational control or whether in fact your evidence is that only this unit of the special police as you named them of the Ministry of Interior were subject to that doctrine. Could you clarify this?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. As is evident from the annual report of the Ministry of Interior for 2001, the Ministry of Interior personnel was not only subject to the process of mobilisation but also was directly involved in combat operations on the ground which resulted in casualties. This is also confirmed by another document which was released by the Ministry of Interior which is the one book of which I'm sure you're well aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. But the question is more limited, if I may, in scope. The question is, is your evidence that the entire Ministry of Interior would have been subjected or would have been liable to this doctrine of operational control which you've used or only the special units of the police of the ministry as you had indicated in your response?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have indicated previously, the specific doctrine of command and control which was applied to the Macedonian security forces is essentially based on three bedrock principles and I mentioned them during my last testimony, I believe. I assume that the same principles as they are reflected in the Law on Internal Affairs apply to the Ministry of Interior including the concept of the operational control, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your answer or your evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko, is that in fact the entire Ministry of Interior was subject to that doctrine. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This would be my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this would view, for instance, the traffic police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The drug police, also, for instance?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know such entity as the drug police. There might be a section in the Ministry of Interior which might be dealing with this issue, but something which would be called exactly as drug police, I have never come across it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would this doctrine of operational control also apply, in your view, to the criminal police?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would this doctrine then also apply to the administrative staff of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would imagine so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. There's another matter which I would like to clarify with you and it is again from your evidence of last week, Mr. Bezruchenko. It's at page 6589 to 6590. And at that page I had asked you whether you agreed with the proposition that to accept your conclusions, again as regard operational control, the Chamber would have to accept that this theory of operational control applied to Mr. Boskoski and to the Ministry of Interior. And in response you had said this: "Yes, I think just for the record perhaps I may say again that in the war situation which was taking place in Macedonia in 2001 the concept of operational control de facto applied both to both components of the Macedonian security forces, these being the Ministry of Interior and the army of the Republic of Macedonia." And the clarification which I seek from you in relation to this response, Mr. Bezruchenko, is this. Is it your evidence that this theory or this doctrine of operational control does not apply to the MOI as a matter of law, but, in your view, de facto. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say that this doctrine actually applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And looking at this from the perspective of an employee of the Ministry of Interior, any employee in view of your previous answer, this would mean that although the employees were not regulated by law by this doctrine, it is your evidence that they should have been aware or they must have been aware of its relevance to their work. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say this. First of all, I believe that the employees of the Ministry of Interior at all times were under the requirements and legislation as emanating from the Law of Internal Affairs, irrespective whether it was war situation or peace situation in the country and I would imagine that under the Law of Internal Affairs, it was their obligation to carry out the proper instructions and orders which might, inter alia, relate to operational control.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we're going to come to the provision. I think it is Article 6 of the Law on Internal Affair to which you have referred but simply to address my question in particular. It is your evidence that despite the fact that this theory or this doctrine of operational control is nowhere to be found in the laws and regulation that applies to the Ministry of the Interior it is your evidence that an employee of the Ministry of Interior should have been aware of the relevance of this doctrine to his or her work. Is that your evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there's another, a last matter of clarification which I would seek from you and it is again from page 6588. It is the transcript of last Friday. You recall you had referred on a number of occasion, both with Mr. Saxon and myself, I believe, to the book, The War of Macedonia. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at some stage in response to one of my question you said this Mr. Bezruchenko and I will read it: "The Ministry of Interior as such as an institution and the Armed Forces of the Republic of Macedonia saw, according to the opinion of these experts an attempt to concur with them the concept of operational control in its military sense will be equally applicable to the entirety of the entity which is called the security forces of Macedonia, being, excuse me, sir, being made up of forces of the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Interior itself as well as the army of the Republic of Macedonia." The clarification which I am seeking from you, Mr. Bezruchenko, and that is not a criticism. It may due to the transcript, but is the suggestion that you make in this particular paragraph that the Macedonian experts, as you call them, have in fact referred to this doctrine of operational control and have in fact suggested that this doctrine applied to the Ministry of Interior, or were you implying something different?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I'm implying is that the experts who have released this book maintain the view that the security forces of Macedonia were indeed made of two components, the army and the Ministry of Interior. And in their entirety as a entity, they were deployed and committed for operations on the ground, meaning that in such operations the principle of operational control applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that this last part of what you have just said is -- does not appear in the book that you have mentioned but is in fact your own conclusions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In other words, there is no suggestion in the book that this doctrine of operational control would have applied to the Ministry of Interior. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the experts and the authors of this book actually speak of the -- what is in Macedonian and B/C/S for that matter is called RiK, rukovodjenje, komandovanje, which is command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we're going to come to the --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- in a moment.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- which is -- yes, yes, sir, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now, we're going to come in in the other concept, Mr. Bezruchenko, in the RiK, the rukovodjenje, komandovanje, but for the time being I would like to stick with the issue of operational control. Can you agree with the suggestion I've put to you that in fact nowhere in the book do these three Macedonian experts, as you call them, refer to the concept of operational control. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they're clearly speaking of the operations which means they're also speaking of the operational control.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree - and I will ask you one more time, Mr. Bezruchenko - that they do not relay on this concept their book. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They don't -- I think they don't mention the phrase like operational control directly in the book but probably they do. I just don't remember. But in whole -- this whole book is about the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that last week we had a little linguistic discussion in relation to the terms operativni and whether it was "operational" or "operative" as we had put it to you. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would it be correct if I put to you that what matter more to this issue is not whether the translation of that word operativni means operational or operative, but more importantly perhaps what it means in the original language. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you will recall that in one particular article, that was Article 154 of the rule of book there was a reference to something called operative control of dangerous areas, which according to you, should be operational control of dangerous areas. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think if I recall correctly I mentioned that operative can be translated two ways in English. It can be translated as quick in terms of quick in reaction and can also be operational, essentially meaning practically the same thing. That is working quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that I had asked you whether you were aware of any internal laws or regulation in which the meaning of this term would be explained and you indicated that you were not aware of any such document. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, speaking of the etymology there is the origin of the word operational and operacionalni, well -- and this is this something which is based on my personal observations. I can simply say in military terminology related to the B/C/S as well as the Macedonian language operacionalni is the word which was taken probably from German or French and can be traced to operational.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But let's --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operational is more like the original form of the word in the B/C/S or in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But let's stick with the term as used by the article in question and also in other documents which is operativni, and let's stay with the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you recall when I asked you whether you were aware of any particular internal rules or regulation which applied at the time or would apply to the Ministry of the Interior and which would explain the accurate or the exact meaning of that concept and you said you didn't. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were discussing it in relation to the document which was entitled the Book of Rules, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. And thereafter --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down and maintain pause between questions and answers, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you recall that after showing you the article in question I had asked whether you were aware of any other document or any other internal regulation or instructions of the Ministry of Interior which would explain or, if you wish, define the meaning of the term as used in this -- in the rule book. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said no to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Bezruchenko. That's what you said. And there's a document that I would like to show to you at this stage and this would be Rule 65 ter 1D940, please. It is it ERN 1D00-8156. The Macedonian version starts at 1D00-8113. Mr. Bezruchenko, can you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, and the title of the document is "Obligatory Instruction."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on the right would you have the Macedonian equivalent of that document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As you can see, this is a document which comes from the secretariat of the internal affairs, it comes from the Ministry of Interior of Macedonia and it is known as "Obligatory Instruction"?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I could ask the registry to please turn to item 31 of that document. That would be page 9 in the English which is 1D00-8164, and in the Macedonian it would start at 1D00-8133, please. And if I can ask the registry to please focus on the bottom of the page, please. Thank you. Mr. Bezruchenko, I'll ask -- I'd like to ask to you focus on item 31 of those instructions of the MOI which refer, as you can see the subheading refers to operative control and you have the version in your -- or not your language, but a language which you also understand, in the Macedonian on the right. And item 31 define operative control in the following terms, and I will read it out to you. "Operative control is a sum of operative-preventative measures that are being taken based on general suspicions and with the aim to prevent criminal acts, following certain persons inclined to commit acts and observation of specific objects and point where criminal acts are committed," and I believe the Macedonian would continue on the next page. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll continue to read the article to you, but at this stage would you agree that this definition of what for the purpose of the MOI constitute operative control does not refer to any military mission or combat activities. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, but I think this article speaks of an entirely different thing. In the sense word "control" here means not necessarily leadership and direction but rather a inspection.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that is quite correct and that was the next question. Would you agree that the expression "operational control" in that context does not refer to a relationship of authority or otherwise between two persons? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It speaks essentially about the police action, police operation, not necessarily a military action but again, as I said, this is a semantic matter again and this article was not even intended to speak about the operational control as you understand in English. It was intended to speak about the police action, police inspection.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that the way in which it is used by and in the Ministry of Interior of Macedonia, do you go with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Macedonian language, yes. Not in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree as well that it doesn't refer to any sort of commanding function. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry perhaps just to read the end of the page. I will go on to read the article, Mr. Bezruchenko. It says: "An object is a place where criminal acts are committed," and if we can please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters would like to kindly ask the witness and the counsel to maintain pauses between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, we have been asked to pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the article goes on to say this: "A point is a place where the perpetrators of criminal acts communicate or where benefit gain through committed criminal acts is being manifested." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you go on to look at the next item or article in this instructions, it says this: "Operative control is established for a person, object or point." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you agree that again this confirm what has been said before is that it does not in this meaning refer in any way so any sort of relationship or authority or commanding function between two people. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it speaks essentially of police action.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that this in fact would appear to be the meaning in which the term was used in Article 154 of the rule book which we had looked at together last week. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that it referred to operative control over dangerous areas. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's another finding --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The document can be removed at this stage. We may come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's another comment or finding which you make in your report which I'd like to turn your attention to, Mr. Bezruchenko. And this is to be found at paragraph 371 of your report. It's page 107 and the exhibit is exhibit P466, please. Do you have that paragraph in front of you, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be page 107, please, in the English. Mr. Bezruchenko, as it appears on the screen, I will read the paragraph to you to refresh your memory. It says this: "Several Macedonian Ministry of Interior documents suggest that Minister of Interior Boskoski exercise operational control of police forces which was manifested in orders to deploy police at various crisis areas." Do you recall making that --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in this paragraph, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- finding? And as indicated in your report in this specific paragraph your finding on that point, namely that in your view, Mr. Boskoski exercised what you called operational control was based on, I believe, 29 different telegrams of redeployment of police forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply to save time, Mr. Bezruchenko, in order to avoid to go through each of these telegrams, would you agree that in effect they are very similar in nature, that they defer in terms of the number of men which are being redeployed, the places where they come from and the locations where they are being deployed. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that you were shown a number of these documents during your examination in chief by Mr. Saxon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps to simplify matter, I will keep to those at this stage and I would like the witness, please, to be shown what is now exhibit P468.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is it under tab 6 of the OTP binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you still have the binder of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to the registry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, that would be tab 6 of the Prosecution binder.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And to refresh your memory a bit about this document, the question that was asked by my colleague Mr. Saxon to you about this particular document was this, and it is the 4th of October 2007, page 6076. And Mr. Saxon asked you this: "Why more security forces were needed at Kumanovo?" Do you recall that question being asked?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in reply you explain the following: "In June 2001 fighting was going on in the area of Kumanovo. In fact the area of Kumanovo was the second front which was opened by NLA sometime in May 2001. So I assume this document indicate that certain reinforcements or replacement of police forces in the area would be required." And then you were asked again in relation to this document whether in your view, this document had any relationship with the issue of operational control which you had discussed earlier with Mr. Saxon, and in answer you said this: "As I mentioned previously, the operational controls involve matters related to organisation and deployment of the forces on the ground. So this is the document which was issued as an exercise of the operational powers by the Ministry of Interior," that's page 6077. Do you recall that, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that you essentially made the same assertions in relation to what is under tab 7, 8 and 9 of the binder, that would be exhibit P469, P470 and exhibit P471. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all these documents are of the same nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if we focus for a moment on this particular document, Mr. Bezruchenko, exhibit P468, do you agree that this document refers specifically to 50 policemen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And will you agree that there is no evidence from this document that these 50 policemen are being redeployed, that are being redeployed were involved at any time in any military or police combat operation. Do you agree that it would not be apparent if that were the case from this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree, I hope, that the document which you have in front of you, the telegram, does not order or does not assign the 50 policemen in question to take part in a military or police operation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say so directly, but if you carefully analyse specifically the second paragraph of this document it would suggest to you that these 50 policemen were not supposed to be transferred to Kumanovo for patrolling streets in the city. They were transferred there to military barracks which apparently served as a assembly area or staging area for operations in the field, and the second paragraph specifically emphasises they should be fully equipped for these kind of operations, they should be in camouflage uniforms, not in dress uniforms, as normally would be the case, they would have to have terrain boots because they would have to run up the mountains, which is a difficult enterprise. They would have to have bullet-proof vests which means there was a fair opportunity for them to come under hostile fire. They would have to have helmets for the same reason. They would have to have masks, sleeping bag, sleeping in the field in a tent. Personal hygiene and spare underwear for a period of at least 15 days. Which means they were supposed to operate in isolation from any sort of facilities in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that in fact from this document at least it is not clear whether this -- any of these 50 policemen ever took part in any operation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Mettraux, it doesn't really say so directly. But the whole concept of military analysis presupposes that you have to put things together rather than relying on one isolated fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So do you agree that here you merely assume in effect that's what happened but this is not in any case evidence from this document. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree -- well, do you agree that in this particular document Mr. Boskoski is not assigning these particular policemen to any particular operation that you would know about. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're specifically referring to the concept of operational control, again, Mr. Mettraux, this document does not necessarily have to say it. It only says that they are supposed to be deployed in the area where military operations were going on. What would happen next, this is an entirely different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that what could happen next is just as likely or just as possible as in fact those 50 policemen carried out regular police duties in the area. We simply do not know from this document. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regular police duties in a war situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, this is your conclusion, Mr. Bezruchenko. But do you agree that this document could be read in such a way that the policemen that were redeployed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, we are a spending a great deal of time. The witness has made clear that the document itself doesn't say so, he has made clear that the second paragraph of the document gives a strong indication. He can take it no further, surely. Why do we keep pressing?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm move on on this one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you agree that this document is sent to the sector in Kocani and more specifically to the sector of finance and other common matters, the sector for analytics and investigation; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was the case with the other documents similar in kind that have you discussed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that in fact all of those documents are telegrams to the effect that police should be replaced, I think you have suggested in your answer to Mr. Saxon that they may be reinforcement but do you agree as far as this document is concerned and I believe the others, it refers to the replacement of forces. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That could be a replacement of forces, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that, Mr. Bezruchenko, the authority or the power that the minister had to deploy or redeploy police forces was an authority or power which you under the Law on Internal Affairs. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly the expression of operational concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree or perhaps you can recall in particular the provision. Would you agree that this is under article 56 of that law, that the minister is able to deploy or redeploy forces, police forces?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I see this article, I would probably confirm this now, but I don't have this document at hand at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I will help you here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could bring exhibit P86.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters kindly ask again the counsel and the witness to make pauses between question and answer and allow interpretation to follow and finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And if I could ask the registry to go to Article 56 of that document, that would be N000-8975 of the English. And N000-8993 of the Macedonian. I would simply like to read out to you this particular provision, Mr. Bezruchenko, Article 56 and it says this: "A employee can be disposed in a organisational unit outside the seat of the ministry with the decision on a post that suits to the employee's professional skills for the following reasons." The first one is "shortage of employees with appropriate professional skills and working abilities for concrete duties and tasks or professional assistance in conducting the duties and tasks of the regional organisational unit and more effect functioning of the ministry." So simply the question, Mr. Bezruchenko, is to confirm that the authority to deploy or redeploy, if you wish, employees of the Ministry of Interior was provided for in this particular provision of the law. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I do not agree with your thesis for one specific reason. To my mind and my reading of this article, is that it addresses purely administrative matters, not operational matters. This article deals with the situations which could be decided on case-by-case basis dealing with the individuals but not entire group of people, 50 men strong with personal arms and equipment to be deployed in a war situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that your evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this provision would prevent the minister to issue such an order or to draft such a telegram based on that provision for more than one individual. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not saying that. I'm only saying that this Article would actually normally apply as the whole of the law to peacetime situations, not wartime situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you state, if your view is different, what provision in your view allowed the minister to seek the redeployment of particular individuals?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 28 of the Law on Defence, which specifically says that the police forces can be deployed to assist the armed forces in the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we're going come back to this article in the context of Article 19 as well. At this stage I would like to show once again to Mr. Bezruchenko what is exhibit P466. That's, again, Mr. Bezruchenko's report. That is page 122, please. And, Mr. Bezruchenko, I'll ask to you look in particular at paragraph 440 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's at page 122.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will read that to you for the record. It says this: "There is at least a few Macedonian Ministry of Interior documents that suggest that minister of the interior Boskoski personally exercised operational control of the unit," and earlier in the section you were talking about the special police unit/posebna, and you go on to say this: "Its control to the unit was manifested in orders to deploy the unit personnel at varies locations." And you say, for example, on 30 July 2001, Boskoski signed a telegram ordering the deployment of 50 policemen of the special police unit to Idrizevo at 7 hours on 2 August to take measures in the territory of Macedonia and to replace a police force." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the footnote which is attached to that particular paragraph and which refers to a document, you will agree that you are referring to a Rule 65 ter document 966 with a ERN N005-0796. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, please, what is the ERN number again?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be footnote 596 in your amended report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see that reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D941, please. Mr. Bezruchenko, this is the -- as you will see, the document to which you make a reference in your report in support of -- of your statement. And this is again you will agree a telegram from -- signed by or on behalf of Mr. Boskoski on the 30th of August of -- of July, I'm sorry, the 30th of July of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the heading, if you wish of the document -- well, first let me ask you this: In your report you suggest that this document is evidence of operative control of the minister over the special unit or Posebna. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that the minister is in fact ordering these Posebna persons to take security measures or are you making a different suggestion?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying here is that, A, these men belong to what is abbreviated here as PEP, Posebna Edinica Policije, special police unit, that these men were deployed to Sokob [phoen], which is apparently training area in the area of Idrizevo and, C, I am saying that they were equipped for operations in the field exactly along the line as the personnel mentioned in similar orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the first matter which I would like you to confirm is, would agree that that telegram is in fact not sent to the members of that Posebna unit but rather to the sector of Veles, and again it's the sector of finance and other common matters and the sector analytics and investigation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree also that at least according to that document, the persons which are concerned by this particular document are not being given any particular tasks or task, I should say, or mission. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you agree perhaps as was the case with the previous version that from that document the -- it is not clear at least from that document that those individuals partook in any police or military operation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't say so, that they're going take part in any police operation or military operation. But one can easily assume reading the paragraph 2 of this document that this was exactly the person-- I mean it was exactly the reason of this operation, to send them to the ground to take part in the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again simply to clarify this, this is your conclusion but that is not what the document says. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusion, sir, is based on the fact of consistency of more than 20 documents of this nature which basically describe the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will ask you in a different way. Do you have any information that any of the 50 policemen concerned by this document in fact took part in a police or military operation of which you would know about?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't have the names of these particular individuals. Otherwise, that would be possible to establish.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in this particular case you have no such information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know again, as I say, the names of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So the answer is no, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my answer, in short, well, to be more precise is that I believe that this document reflects the operational matter, deployment of personnel. The reason why it is addressed to sector of finance and common matters is that apparently such orders had to be accompanied through appropriate measures through financial channels. That is, these men had to be paid certain allowances, field allowances or combat allowances. And the reason why it is addressed to sector of internal affairs, Veles, is that this sector was supposed to provide a number of personnel for the special unit and we know that in fact the special police unit as it is commonly called as Posebna is a composite unit which was tailored on the basis of need to address specific situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just to follow up on your answer, the responsibility to prepare that group, if you so wish, of 50 policemen would in turn be with the sector of Veles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be logical to assume, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Staying for a moment with the special unit there is another paragraph which I would like to draw your attention upon. Again, from your report. And that would be paragraph 403 and this would be again Exhibit 466, the report of Mr. Bezruchenko. Mr. Bezruchenko, this would be at page 111 of your report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to draw your attention to paragraph 403, where you make a reference to a passage of Mr. Bolton's statement. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your report you rely upon the particular statement and it is the first sentence of that quote and it says this: "It is my belief, "Mr. Bolton's belief, "that normal practice when employing police special units in a pre-planned operation is for the plan to be developed at a senior level." And he goes on to say --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes on to say -- he goes on to say this: "Normally the minister would be involved into this planning process but if it were not to be due to the centralised nature of the ministry both in 2001 and at the present time and due to the potential political and security implication of such an operation, he would," and if we can turn to the next page, "demand to be fully briefed and informed by his staff." And Mr. Bolton expressed a further view that "I would find it hard to conceive of a situation in which the minister during the operation of the conflict in 2001 was not informed beforehand of any pre-planned tactical operation by special or irregular police units." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall however that in his evidence Mr. Bolton indicated that at the time he had not met with Mr. Boskoski. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware perhaps that there was evidence led in this courtroom to the effect that the minister did not in fact take part in the planning of operation of the special units, and I think the evidence was led in particular in relation to the Tigers unit. Would you be aware of that evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm only aware of what I have written in my report, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that with a view to amend and update your report, Mr. Bezruchenko, you have made reference or references to a number of passage from the transcript of this trial. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as part of your review to update or amend your report did you become aware of the evidence of a particular witness that indicated that the minister did not take part in the planning of operation of the Tigers unit?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was following the proceedings of the case, of course, and there were numerous witnesses who were testifying on varies points related to the functioning and responsibilities. Well, if the implication of the question is why the selection of my materials for the report was determined by this other factor, then the answer is that this is essentially the concept which I was following which was formulated in my mind throughout the examination of the entirety of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But simply to clarify, Mr. Bezruchenko, simply whether or not you were aware of that evidence to the effect that Mr. Boskoski in fact did not take part in the planning of operations involving the Tigers unit.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could be more specific, please, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I will read out to you the evidence in that case. It comes from the transcript of the 15th of June of 2007 and it is the evidence of M-056. The page, I believe, is 2167 and the evidence or the question, rather, was that: "The minister of the interior in one such situation had no role in the planning or the execution of that operation. Is that correct". The answer is: "Yes, it is correct." The question is: "Even if he would be present at the meeting that the execution of that plan he would have no authority to issue any orders or directions or suggestions to the army generals; is that correct?" "Yes." And the question simply, Mr. Bezruchenko, is whether or not you were aware of that evidence.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could kindly remind of the name of the witness, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we should go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps just to ask you the question again for the record, Mr. Bezruchenko. Were you or were you not aware of this particular piece of the evidence when amending and completing your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of this evidence, but I would find it hard to believe that a person who would be on equal footing with the minister of defence, having a number of police generals under him, would not be in a position at least to issue recommendations to his military counterparts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But staying for a minute with the evidence of M-056, do I understand your answer to suggest that you disregarded the evidence of this person for the purpose of amending your report because you found this evidence hard to believe? Is that your evidence or did I misunderstand your interpretation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not that I disregarded this evidence. Otherwise I did not select this evidence for the sake of amending the report, because, as I say, the evidence which I use in my report has to be evaluated in terms of credibility and value and to my criteria which I establish for myself, when writing this report, this was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your evidence in relation to that particular piece of the evidence and more generally to the material which you say you have relied upon for the purpose of amending the indictment you are saying, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you exercised your own judgment as to the reliability or otherwise and credibility or otherwise of the evidence before relying upon in your in report. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have been relying mainly and I specifically made a point for myself to rely mainly, if not exclusively, on the documents which would provide hard, strong and valuable evidence related to the actual situation on the ground. Well, obviously in cases where there was no specific evidence as reflected in the documents, specific to very specific points in fact cannot be corroborated in other ways, I had to use some of witness statements, but I believe there are very, very few.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you did or felt had you to rely upon a statement, or I'm sorry, upon the evidence of a witness, you, as you indicated, exercised your own judgment as to what you believe to be the reliability, credibility and I believe you use the word value of that evidence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that -- or perhaps I should ask you this. How many plans of operations, police operations or military operations have you seen that bear the signature of Mr. Buckovski [Realtime transcript read in error "Boskoski"]?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Plans of military operations, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what about plans of police combat operations?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that the statement - and if you don't know this, Mr. Bezruchenko, simply indicate it - but are you aware of the fact that the statement of Mr. Bolton on which you relied for the suggestion that the witness had used the expression "operational control" had been taken by your colleague Mr. Kuehnel. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of this fact, but that would not be anything extraordinary.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in his evidence Mr. Bolton was asked to explain these paragraphs, these particular paragraphs of his statement and in particular he was asked to explain his belief that members of the MOI would sometimes defer to Mr. Boskoski for decision concerning issues that involved low-level tactical policing. Do you recall that part of his evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that he explained that this belief that he had was based on two incidents: One about the moving or removing of a particular police check-point, and another one about the timing of police shifts. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that in his evidence Mr. Bolton made it clear that he never been able to verify the truth of what he had been told about these two matters. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about this particular point.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel and the witness to observe a pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But will you recall perhaps, Mr. Bezruchenko, that at the time Mr. Bolton indicated that as regard the first incident, which would be the adjustment of the police shift, he was or he said he had been told by Mr. Bliznakovski and Mr. Jovanovski. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I recall this particular -- this particular situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you recall that under questions by counsel he explained that the basis of his belief had never been verified or is it something that lies beyond your awareness?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be very difficult for me to refer to a witness statement and give my opinion about what was said in which I was not really involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, Your Honour, perhaps to simplify I will simply give the reference to the record of relevant part. This is the transcript of 8th of June 2007. It is page 1777 to 1780. But perhaps I can put that proposition to you, Mr. Bezruchenko. Is it your expert evidence that the removal or the moving of a particular police check-point in one location, or the changing or accommodation of the timing of the police shift would be relevant illustrations of what is known as the military doctrine of operative control. Is that your view that such incident would be indication of what you termed "operative control." Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: More on the tactical level, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would be regardless, in your view, of the reasons for the particular check-points or the basis for the police shift. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm a little bit at a loss how to explain the reason of your using the word "regardless." Obviously there are always reasons for certain tactical steps to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You're right about my question, Mr. Bezruchenko. Would you give the same answer, namely that the placing of a check-point or the changing police shift would be relevant to what you say is operative control, whether the reason for the placing of such check-point or the changing of the police shift would be military in kind, policing in kind, or for any other particular reason such as the convenience, perhaps, of other international organisation or that of the police employees, would your answer be the same in all of those cases?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. I would only say that the mere presence of a police check-point in the country in the crisis area during the war situation would indicate to me the fact that this check-point was erected in this particular location for a certain reason which was not explained by anything else but a military situation. Or perhaps the consideration of safety and security.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you draw those conclusions about the reason of the presence of a particular check-point or police forces - or I'm sorry - of police shift, you are not relying upon the evidence of Mr. Bolton, or are you, on that point?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is just my general comment. I can not really rely on anyone's statement. As I said while in my report I used mainly documents and those appropriate or those relevant paragraphs from various statements that I quote in my report were quoted there for reasons which I hope I stated previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that in your report, Mr. Bezruchenko, you have cited no one order signed by Mr. Boskoski which related specifically to a police operation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. We have just discussed a number of those orders which were signed by Mr. Boskoski which are directing police forces for redeployment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I thank you for this qualification. But setting aside the orders of redeployment, do you agree that you have cited no particular orders or plans signed by Mr. Boskoski which would relate to a police operation in the meaning that is understood in military doctrine. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree that the reason perhaps why you saw no such documents - and I will come back to this perhaps later today or tomorrow - is that at the time the Law on Defence gave the power to order the use of police forces in combat either to the president under the old law or the president of the government, that would be the prime minister under the new law. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The powers to use police in support of military operations were mentioned in both the new law which I think was adopted sometime in early June 2001 and in the previous law as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that the change that were brought from the old law to the new law - and as I said I will show to you the relevant provision later today - but if you can agree with this general proposition, the change which was brought between the old law which placed the authority to use police forces in support of military combat or activities was in the hands of the president of the Republic of Macedonia, whereas the new law which, as you said, was adopted, I believe, on the 1st of June placed that responsibility in the hands of the president of the government, which is the prime minister. Can you agree with that general proposition?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this general proposition is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps you've indicated also that you have indicated your reason for referring to a number of witnesses with a view to update your report for the purpose of these proceedings. Were you aware of the fact that a number of witnesses of the Prosecution had given evidence to the effect that the Ministry of Interior had in fact no operational powers of responsibility as regard the activities of the police in the field? Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember some statements to this regard, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you indicate if and where you amended your indictment -- I'm sorry, your report with a view to allow for this evidence to be taken into consideration?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was amending my report on the basis of new sources and again these were mainly documentary evidence. These were mainly documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So can I understand your response to suggest that in fact you did not refer in your report to the evidence which was led to the effect that the minister had no operational role?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned previously, throughout the process of preparation of my report and selection of the sources for the report, I was guided by major overriding consideration of providing the best possible sources which mainly included documents trying to avoid any speculative statements as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And so in answer to the question, and perhaps you can answer this one simply, do you agree that have you not made any reference in the amended version of your report to these particular statements that were made by a number of Prosecution witness to the effect that the minister had no operational control. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't refer to these statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I could ask the registry please to bring up once again Mr. Bezruchenko's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I will ask you to look at page 111 of your report, please. This is exhibit P466, I apologise. And I will draw your attention in particular, Mr. Bezruchenko, to what is paragraph 401 of that report. Can you locate it?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will just read the paragraph in question for the record, the statements which you make here. It says this: "A few Macedonian government documents suggest that at a late stage of the conflict, the government made an attempt to create a provisional joint anti-terrorist unit. The decision to create this unit was apparently meant to fill the drastic demand for units trained in special anti-terrorist operations. The joint anti-terrorist unit was tailored from army elements and Ministry of Interior special police units. Thus, on 6 August 2001, minister of interior Boskoski signed an order authorising the transfer of "Tigers" and "Lions" special police unit (together, the joint police unit) into the newly created joint anti-terrorist unit." And then you say the following: "This decision suggests that minister exercised his powers to control the operations of the special police units." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply to understand this last statement of yours properly, Mr. Bezruchenko, is that your evidence again that this particular document to which you refer, and that would be exhibit P275, is again evidence of operational control on the part of the minister and this time in particular operational control in relation to the special police units.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I see the document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Bezruchenko. This would be exhibit P275.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The document, Your Honour, is referring footnote 560, I believe, of Mr. Bezruchenko's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have the document in front of you, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So simply to understand the evidence which you are giving in relation to this document, is that your evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this particular order as signed by Minister Boskoski would, as you say in your report, demonstrate the power of the minister to control the operation of the police units. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So is that your evidence that the assignment or transfer or appointment of individuals to a particular unit yet to be formed would in itself be evidence of operational control? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Macedonian this document is titled somewhat differently than it is translated in effect. I would rather put it as the order for definition of the units of the Ministry of Interior which are supposed to be included into the provisional joint unit to fight against terrorism. But in any case, the point about this document is that the Minister of Interior makes a decision as to which units which are within the Ministry of Interior and therefore under his purview are supposed to be released and included into the ministry -- I mean, included into this temporary unit to fight against terrorism, which is, again, an operational decision. Basically the Ministry of Interior transfers the command of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So is your evidence on this point this, that the assignment or the release, as you termed it, of individuals to a different body, in this case, a joint unit, would itself be evidence of the minister's actual control over the operations of the individuals who are being released? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying that. I'm not saying that this is a indication of the operational control of individuals. I am saying that this is an indication of the operational control of individuals. I am saying that this is the evidence operational control to the unit, which is changing hands which comes from under the Ministry of Interior into the temporary joint unit for combat against terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. Perhaps my question was not very clear. But is it your evidence that the power to assign an individual to or to release an individual to the different -- to a different unit would or could also serve as evidence in your case of that person's power to control the operations of the special unit in question? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, I can't -- I don't quite understand what you exactly mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the question is not very clear. But you will agree that this order has to do with the assignment or the release of individuals. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a unit, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this particular document does not refer or does not relate to any particular operation to which these individuals are to be involved in. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the transfer of authority of the unit and its release or, if you wish, inclusion into another body, is in itself an operational action because it implies transfer of operational control.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So simply to be clear and I want to be very clear on this, Mr. Bezruchenko, it is your view as an expert that the power or the authority which the minister had in this case to reassign or to release, as you said, individuals, is also evidence of his power to control the particular unit in question. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. At least he has been controlling this unit, well, up to this point, and he probably preserved that means [indiscernible] disciplinary control of this unit beyond this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree in fact, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this particular joint unit was never set up. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not necessarily the fact. I have seen at least several documents which imply that joint anti-terrorist unit was involved in operations in the area of Tetovo at a late stage of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that when you prepared your original report at the least you were informed by the minister of the Defence that this particular joint unit to which this document refers was never set up. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had that document from the minister of defence which, indeed, stipulated that such a unit was never established. But this was only a verbal statement of him, which was not supported by any documents. Now I can see a number of documents which clearly speak about the existence of such unit. To which point this unit was actually functional and operational on the ground is entirely different matter. But as I mentioned, and I would like to put again, I saw at least some documents which suggest that this unit was operational was committed into action in the area of Tetovo in later stage of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that when you interviewed the minister of defense Mr. Boskoski as you just mentioned, he had indicated to that in fact this joint unit had never been set up, and would you also agree with the proposition that this particular statement of Mr. Boskoski which had been entered in your original report has disappeared from the amended report? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have removed it from the amended report because I found documents which actually negated this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, if you look perhaps at the preamble of that document, do you agree that this particular order signed by Mr. Boskoski refers to two earlier documents or to a earlier decision, I should say, one by the government and one by the president. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the record, the decision of the government is Exhibit 1D59 and the decision of the president is Exhibit 1D60. And my attention is drawn to the transcript, paragraph 39, line 14 which referred to a particular statement of Mr. Boskoski. It should be Mr. Buckovski. My attention is also being drawn, Your Honour, on the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that convenient to you, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, then, we will adjourn until quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you recall that just before the break we were discussing the order of the 6th of August concerning the joint unit. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall making the suggestion that this particular order of Mr. Boskoski was, in your view, indicative of what you call his operational control. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was an act of transferring the operational control from -- of this unit to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that this order which Mr. Boskoski was issuing on the 6th of August of 2001, was in fact based and done pursuant to two decisions. I think we've talked about this already. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand this was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those two decisions were respectively a decision of the government of the 12th of June 2001 and of the president of the republic of 15th of June 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document seems to suggest that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that these two decisions which have just been mentioned were binding on Mr. Boskoski. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree also that according to the content of these two decisions by the government and the president respectively, the only matter that was left to Mr. Boskoski to decide was the composition of the unit that was to be transferred to the joint unit. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be grateful to Your Honour if you could help me with taking a look at these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Which one do you -- well, perhaps I should show you chronologically, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we could see the decision of first the government of the Republic of Macedonia. That would be Exhibit 1D59, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document, Mr. Bezruchenko? Perhaps to assist you, the actual decision is attached on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if Mr. Bezruchenko may be shown the second page of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I saw this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps briefly I'll go with you through the document in question and that may or may not assist your recollection. If you look at the first paragraph. It's the decision that is referred to in the preamble of the decision of the 6th of August of 2001. First paragraph says this: "The decision approves the formation of a special purpose unit for halting and combatting terrorist actions on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the second paragraph it says - it's paragraph 2 - "The ranks of the special purpose unit will be composed of army units which will be selected by the president with a separate resolution and police units which will be selected by the Ministry of the Interior with the separate order." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps before we proceed with the other document as well. Can you recall or is it within your knowledge that the actual authority to use and control the new foreseen special unit or joint unit was to remain with the president of the republic. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember seeing some documents which suggested the president of the republic was exercising control over the army and police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, specifically about this joint unit perhaps I should draw your attention to paragraph 6, please, Mr. Bezruchenko. Can you see it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says this: "The order for the use of the special purposes unit will be issued by the president on the recommendation of the coordinated body for crisis management." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can now turn to what is Exhibit 1D60, please. And perhaps I should have asked you this before leading the document. Was it a document that was within your knowledge, Mr. Bezruchenko, before it was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you can now focus on the next document, which is -- which appears in front of you. Do you recognise this document as being the decision of the 15 of June 2001 signed by the president of the republic and which is referred to in the preamble of the order of the 6th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the second page of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can focus your attention on point 1.2, please, which is the part that is addressed to the Ministry of the Interior, specifically it says this: "The formation of a special tasks unit and its incorporation into the special operations detachment. The composition of the session tasks unit is to be determined by the Ministry of Interior. Then the formation of a police battalion in the ranks of the Ministry of Interior that will be incorporated into the anti-terrorism unit, the composition of the battalion is to be determined by the Ministry of the Interior." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
