utterances.text: And do you agree -- perhaps I will use an image that in these two orders by the -- or decisions issued by the government and then by the president, what is being asked of the Ministry of Interior is to choose, if you wish, from a deck of card, what unit or what composition should be transferred to the new joint unit. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know to which extent this could be an appropriate comparison, but I don't really think that the Ministry of Interior had so many units at its disposal as to compare them to a deck of cards.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I suppose that depends on the game of card we are playing. But would you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, in any case that what is left for the minister of the interior to decide is the composition of the unit. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. I think the point, the main point of this document as far as the Ministry of Interior is concerned, is that this police battalion, is yet to be formed. Well, reading the document, I'm getting an impression that it speaks of some units, mainly military units, which have already been in existence, like the first [indiscernible] Brigade, for instance, and the yet-to-be-composed units of the Ministry of Interior such as the police battalion in the ranks of the MVR. What leads me to make this conclusion is paragraph 4 in fact, on the first page of this document which clearly speaks of formation of the police battalion in the ranks of the Ministry of Interior which will be incorporated, will be incorporated. So the formation apparently didn't even exist at the point of this document being released.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But just discussing, Mr. Bezruchenko, the relationship between this particular decision which you have in front of you together with the decision of the government that I showed to you a moment ago, and on the other hand, the order of the 6th of August, you will agree, I hope, that the principle that a number of individuals or particular units should be transferred from the Ministry of the Interior to a new joint unit had already been decided by the government and the decision of the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Apparently the concepts of the unit was already in place and the process of establishing such a unit was initiated. However, I would like to draw your attention, Mr. Mettraux, again, to the date of 6 August 2001, which is the date when the actual decision about the release of the special police unit was signed. Apparently this is the date when this unit actually entered into the composition of the unit for special purposes or as a anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the decision which was left to the Ministry of Interior as regard the new joint unit was as the document in front of you suggests, a decision as to the composition of the units or unit which should come from the Ministry of the Interior into the joint unit. Do you agree with that, on the basis of 1.2 of that document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends on which date.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that the date at which the order was rendered by the minister of the interior is the 6th of August of 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that at that time the decision which the minister had to take and which he took in fact in light of the two other decisions which he cite was one of the units to be transferred to the joint unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that in fact he was exercising the operational control of this unit exactly up to this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that the principle as to the transfer and I think you have read it or you have said it already, had been decided by the minister or the government and then by the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say not the principle but, rather, the executive decision was already in the making.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as you indicated, that those decisions were binding on Mr. Boskoski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's another matter, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you discussed with Mr. Saxon in connection or, rather, following the discussion of this issue of operational control and I would like to turn our attention to this now. And this is the issue of discipline, disciplinary issue. Do you recall discussing this with Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in paragraph 3337, that is at pages 118 to 120 of your report, you discuss some aspects of these questions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there's a number of general questions that I want to ask you at this stage, and the first one is -- I think you have indicated it in two places in your report, at paragraph 424 and 429 of the report that the disciplinary powers to which you refer in your report in so far as relevant to these proceedings relate to -- are called violations of labour discipline. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And because the issue of the structure particularly the disciplinary matter of the Ministry of Interior lies beyond your expertise, I will not direct our attention specifically to this but to some more general statements which you've made in your evidence and I would like to bring yourself back to those statements. And I will simply summarize them to ensure that I have an accurate understanding of your evidence. You've indicated, I believe, the page 6070, that's the 4th of October of 2007, that in a military setting the organ or person competent to enforce disciplinary standards would normally be the superior of the commander who would the operational control. Is that an accurate summary of what you said?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily sir. Actually let me explain it again. I will try to make it very brief and very clear. We should not really mix up the operational control and administrative control of which the discipline is a function. Operational control relates to everything which is essentially war making function, that is actual fighting. Administration is everything which relates -- which actually does not relate to fighting and which serves in support of operational control and fighting. Discipline as well as other matters is in fact a functional area of administration. So if we are talking about the enforcing of disciplinary standards it really depends on the specific situation and the specific level of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And thank you for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just before we go any further, I'd like to indicate that at line 10 of page 47, my colleague said the following as a preamble to his last question: "And because the question of the structure, particularly the disciplinary matter of the Ministry of the Interior lies beyond your expertise," and then he continued. Just simply for the record, Your Honour, Prosecution believes this is a matter for the Trial Chamber to draw a conclusion on, not my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, there is another comment or statement that you made that I would like to bring yourself back to and this is - and again correct me if the summary is inaccurate. You said that, and I quote: "In a normal military structure," superiors generally have disciplinary powers over subordinates, and I believe you said that the issue of discipline would be addressed by someone higher up in the line of command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid this has to be qualified, sir. What exactly do you know, which line of command and which level of command?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I would wish to ascertain from you, Mr. Bezruchenko, is the suggestion or the apparent suggestion that the responsibility for disciplinary matters would normally or necessarily, as the case may be, lie with a superior of the person who committed the violations of labour discipline within his line of command or line of authority. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me describe it in the following way. Suppose I'm a commander of a unit and one of my soldiers commits a crime or a breach of discipline. I have the obligation under the doctrine of full command being fully responsible for everything happening in my unit to take care about this event, meaning I have to make an investigation if I have the appropriate powers, of course, and take the appropriate measures. But depending on the situation and depending on the exact disciplinary powers that a military commander has at each level of the hierarchical structure, it is not necessarily the immediate superior of the -- of mine who is supposed to take care of a situation if I commit a crime or a breach of discipline. What I'm trying to say is that this is not really a dogma. This is a doctrine which has flexible application.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. That was my next question or my next proposition for you. Would you agree that the responsibility or otherwise in a military outfit or a military structure would depend on the particular structure of that body and I think, as you've indicated, the responsibility for taking care of such matter will and otherwise might depend from the military structure in question. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally this is the case, yes. Normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree also that in some military settings or that you may or may know [sic] about the responsibility to inquire, investigate or otherwise punish disciplinary breaches would be assigned to a specific organ of the military whose responsibility is to take care of this. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are varies organs for these kind of activities in various armies. In former JNA it was military faculties and military costs, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. And you would agree that for a particular line of command or a particular chain of command within the military, for that particular line of command to be responsible to take disciplinary action, it would have to be established in the first place, and I may state the obvious, but that a disciplinary offence has been committed within that structure, within that line. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. Allegations would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. And the allegation which you say would be sufficient or the actual commission of a breach would have to be committed by an individual to be found within that particular line or chain of command. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, put it this way: A military commander has a responsibility of his men in his command. If, say, a breach of discipline would be committed by a neighbouring unit, well, he would not really have direct authority over these men.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful. You corrected or you made the answer clearer than the question, which is that a particular commander would not have disciplinary responsibility in relation to breaches committed by individuals who are in a different line of or chain of command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Wouldn't that last answer, though, Mr. Bezruchenko, be subject to the basis upon which a person is subjected temporarily to the command of somebody? He may be fully subjected and therefore fully subjected to disciplinary authority of the person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, sir. Well, in fact it is not an unusual development, especially in a war situation, whenever a unit is under a provisional command or perhaps being attached on a temporary basis to another unit of which there is an established commander, this commander would exercise a disciplinary powers over this unit including these men, but having said that, as a rule and as a matter of fact, the administrative and disciplinary authorities would be retained by the commander of the unit to which these men originally belonged to. What I am trying to say, this again comes back to the distinction between operational and disciplinary control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I intervened, Mr. Mettraux, because I thought the witness was saying something quite different from what I had understood from his previous evidence but I see we -- I correctly understood exactly what he was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I hope it may have helped you as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, if we transfer the evidence which you've given in relation to the military structure in this case to the situation of the Ministry of the Interior, you would agree, I hope, that for anyone within the Ministry of Interior to have any type of disciplinary duties or responsibilities, it would first have to be established that the breach of labour discipline was in fact committed by a member of that ministry or you said that there were allegations to that effect. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It probably would depend on the specific situation on the ground. I don't think there is a general rule which would really govern these kinds of situations. But, again, as a general rule, I would say that there should be sufficient grounds to warrant an investigation or perhaps at least to make a decision as to disciplinary action.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But if you can focus, Mr. Bezruchenko, on the other part of my question more specifically, do you agree if for the Ministry of Interior, anyone within that ministry to have any duty or responsibility as regards violations of the discipline, it would have to be established in the first place that the person who committed that breach was in fact a member of the ministry. In other words, the Ministry of Interior would have no duty to discipline someone who was not a de jure member of the ministry. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that in the course of the investigation of this case, you've interviewed quite a number of witnesses?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't term it this way, Mr. Mettraux. I have no authority to interview anyone, but I was involved in the interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for the correction, Mr. Bezruchenko. But you would agree also that on a number of occasion you actually put questions to witnesses. Do you agree that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the investigator, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply as a matter of clarification, Mr. Bezruchenko, is it your evidence that you actually never directly addressed a question to a interviewee or are you suggesting anything else?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, my questions were addressed through the investigator. But as we were talking, perhaps some of the questions could be understood or implied to be understood by a interviewee as a direct question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact you asked the question directly; it was not investigator that asked them on your behalf, is that correct? On a number of occasion you asked the question directly of the witness and got a direct answer from the witness. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I think there could be such instances, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as part of your involvement in this matter, you also reviewed, and I think it is quite clear in your evidence, a relatively large number of documents pertaining to these proceedings. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, which proceedings do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in the context of the investigation of this case, both prior and after the indictment of Mr. Boskoski and Mr. Tarculovski, you did review a number of document, including documents that became exhibits as part of your work as a military analyst. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, this is my job description to review these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as part of this process of investigating the case and reviewing documents and taking part in various interviews, you became aware, didn't you, of some serious difficulties which the Prosecution had to determine whether the people whom you thought might have committed crimes in Ljuboten were in fact members of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I would put it this way. My job was to analyse the conflict and those aspects of the conflict which were essential for its description. As to the actual investigation, investigation leads an investigation clues and investigation tactics, it is not really my business and wasn't really involved in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bezruchenko, I'm putting it to you that you personally became aware of serious problems which related to this very matter, namely the fact that individuals who you believed might have been responsible for the crimes in or around Ljuboten were in fact not members of the Ministry of the Interior. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not, sir. Well, I am not aware that I was aware of any serious problems and as I say, again, the investigation is something that was not really my primary concern. My primary concern was doing precisely what I was supposed to do. That is providing the description of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting it to you that those concerns related in particular to concerns which you expressed to colleagues that in the absence of clear evidence that those who you believed to have committed the crimes were members of the Ministry of Interior, you would be hard put to establish a line of command between Mr. Boskoski and those person, and you also expressed the view to your colleague that as a result of that, you would encountered difficulties proving Mr. Boskoski's disciplinary duties in relation to these people. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have been having, well, my views on certain documents, and certain aspects of the description of the conflict, but that does not necessarily mean that I actually expressed anything like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we're going to come back in a minute to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Even assuming for the sake of argument that Mr. Bezruchenko had made such expressions, is my colleague suggesting that if he did make them, such a honesty evaluation of information available to him would somehow affect the credibility of his evidence? Because if not, I don't know what the relevance of this line of questioning is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I think the answer has been given by the witness. He has indicated that he never made any such comment, Your Honour. And the Defence will, in a moment, return to a document which in fact might suggest a slightly different involvement of Mr. Bezruchenko than the one claimed, and also a particular position taken about a number of issue which we submit would be directly relevant to the credibility or otherwise of the witness. As far as the statements are concerned, Mr. Bezruchenko has indicated that he did not make such statement and described his involvement in matters of the description of the conflict and not in investigative matters. We believe, Your Honour, that this is a proper course of cross-examination, particularly in light of the Trial Chamber which indicated that those matters could be pursued as a matter of weight and credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You say the relevance is credibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is credibility, Your Honour, and also we believe weight, if any, to be given to several aspects of the report of Mr. Bezruchenko. We would wish, if permitted, not to indicate too much at this stage in front of the witness, but we would indicate that this would also, in our submission, be relevant to the weight to be given, if any, to some parts, at least, of the report of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Anything further, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's difficult to see how such evidence, if it exists, would be relevant to weight to be given to certain parts of Mr. Bezruchenko's report because as Mr. Bezruchenko has testified, he was tasked to analyse the armed conflict if it existed in Macedonia in 2001 and the parties to that armed conflict. He was not tasked to analyse whether certain persons who may or may not have been in Ljuboten on the 12th of August were members of the Ministry of Interior. That certainly was not part of the scope of his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At least on the basis of credibility, there seems -- on what is presently known to be and on the assurance of Mr. Mettraux, there seems to be some adequate basis for the questioning to pursue. What, if anything, can be made of the outcome of that, this is something which as far as the Chamber is concerned, is entirely conjectural at the time. The issue may become clearer as the questioning is pursued and it may be necessary for the Chamber then to intervene. But, for the moment, please continue, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour. And my apologies, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that when you became aware of difficulties with the identification of those believed to have committed crimes in Ljuboten and more specifically, the difficulties to establish that these persons were in fact de jure members of the MOI, the decision was taken to pursue a course of evidence whereby members of special units of the MOI were said to have been present in Ljuboten. Is it something within the realm of your knowledge, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it within the realm of your knowledge that for the same reason, the decision was -- or the course was pursued to suggest that the special units of the Ministry of Interior all those which you said existed at the time were under the direct control and command of Mr. Boskoski? Is it something which is within the realm of your knowledge or ...

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me put it this way, sir. The fact of the crimes committed in Ljuboten as well as the perpetrators was not really the subject of my report. Had it been, there should have been a special section which would have been devoted to the crimes committed as well as the suspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Bezruchenko, that at least until -- or perhaps I should ask you this. Is this correct that until well into the year of 2005, that is after the indictment of Mr. Boskoski, there remained doubts within your office as to whether the people who were alleged to have committed the crimes or believed to have committed the crimes in -- in and around Ljuboten were in fact regular police officers or irregulars. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. If there were such doubts, well, at least I was not aware of those and besides, as I say, even if these doubts existed, it wouldn't have affected my report since the subject of crimes was not within the scope of what I was describing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D937.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, what I'm about to show you is a so-called investigator's notes and it's an investigator's note of Mr. Stojance Bogeski, and it is dated the 26th of June of 2005. Can you see that on your screen?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may draw your attention to the subheading which says purpose of interview, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the interview --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may draw your attention to the last sentence of that document -- of that paragraph, I apologise, it says this: "In addition, the person could assist the ICTY in recognition of identity of the regular or irregular groups of Macedonians involved in Ljuboten operation." So first I should ask you whether you were aware of these particular investigator's notes?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could probably go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The note, Mr. Bezruchenko, was taken by Mr. Lubomir Josefciak.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't see the implication of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you agree that at least as late as 26th of June 2005 the Office of the Prosecutor was still seeking to establish whether the individuals believed to have committed crimes as part of the Ljuboten information were regular or irregular groups of Macedonians. Do you agree that's what the note suggestions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution will stipulate that well into the spring of 2006 the Trial Chamber, the former Trial Chamber compelled the Prosecution to identify additional members of the JCE as it was described in its indictment in the Prosecution's second amended indictment and its amended pre-trial brief. Having said that, what then is the relevance of the fact that the Prosecution was continuing its investigation to try to identify further at this point in the summer of 2005, tried -- to try to identify with more precision who were the individuals who were part of the Ministry of Interior who were in Ljuboten village on the weekend of the 10th to the 12th of August? How is that relevant to the testimony of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to Mr. Saxon' submission, the issue here, I believe, is not one, at least not the one that was being explored, of the fact that the Prosecution was continuing to seek to investigate this matter which, as Mr. Saxon indicated, is completely proper. The question was that of the knowledge of the particular witness of that fact, which has now been explored with him and whether he was aware of these particular facts, namely that the Prosecutor had or was still seeking at the time to identify the particular individuals involved. If Your Honour believes that the question is too remote, since the witness has indicated that he hasn't participated in this particular interview, although he's indicated he knew about the notes, I will ask him specifically about the interviews to which he participated and which would be relevant, we submit, to the matters indicated earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it certainly is not apparent that this document will advance the matter, Mr. Mettraux. If you say there is other material that comes nearer to relevance, we will look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, and the document may be removed at this stage. Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that one of the interviews to which you personally participated was the interview of former minister of defence Mr. Vlado Buckovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that during that particular interview Mr. Buckovski told the investigator or the team of the Office of the Prosecutor that the group that was in Ljuboten on the 10, 11 and 12 or during that weekend, did not belong to the regular security forces. Do you have a memory of Mr. Buckovski telling you this?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can assist you with --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's Rule 65 ter 1D856, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can first focus on the first page of that document, Mr. Bezruchenko. Can you -- it's, as you can see, the record of interview of the minister of defence of Macedonia, Vlado Buckovski, and it list two interviewers as being Matti Raatikainen and Viktor Bezruchenko. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would be yourself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can please turn to the second page of that document. And if I can ask to you look at paragraph 8 of that document. Is that correct that Mr. Buckovski expressed the view that the group in question did not belong to the regular security forces?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that the -- it can -- it can be removed at this stage. Is that correct that Mr. Buckovski also explained to you that the matter of this group had been raised directly with the prime minister at the time. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall something like that, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that on another occasion in a different interview -- I should ask you that way. Is it correct that during the interview of Mr. Sasa Isovski, a member of the army, he was asked about whether a number of persons had been in Ljubanci and Ljuboten during the particular weekend and whether they had been members of that security agency. Can you recall that being asked of him?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. And if I can comment at this point. I think that the investigation was actually exploring all opportunities and was open to all actions in a completely impartial and neutral way and therefore all these scenarios of what happened in Ljuboten were being explored.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you also recall that when the matter was raised in particular with Mr. Sasko Isovski as to whether he could rather any of those men present in the area at the time, he explained to you that he was unable to distinguish between members of the police and member of that agency, because who were in uniform. Can you recall that he told you this?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that actually he was asked questions as to the identity of this man, perhaps, as far as I can recall, but I'm not entirely certain what his answer was, and even if he had given some specific answer that matter -- that the matter would not stop at this point in the process of an investigation. There certainly would be other investigating matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you cannot personally recall whether - or I should ask you that - where you cannot recall what answer Mr. Isovski gave you in relation to this particular question. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember his specific answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that the prime minister himself, Mr. Ljubco Georgievski, whom defence minister Mr. Buckovski had mentioned to you also told your office when interviewed that he did not know what forces had been involved in this matter. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Georgievski, if I recall correctly, was interviewed by ICTY investigators, but I'm not involved in this interview and I'm not -- I cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D865, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you -- do you have the statement in front of you, Mr. Bezruchenko, that is the OTP statement of Ljubco Georgievski?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Which Georgievski do you mean? You mean the prime minister?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could please turn to page 7 of that document. That would be page 1D00-724, please. And I will ask the registry to focus on page 46 of that document. Mr. Bezruchenko, this is what then prime minister or in any case the prime minister in 2001 told the Office of the Prosecutor: "Being asked what kind of Macedonian forces participated in the operation in Ljuboten, I say I do not know." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you have that particular statement in your possession when preparing the report that you have prepared?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you familiar with this particular statement in the report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I was quoting this statement in my report, no. As I mentioned previously I was trying as much as possible to avoid relying on any statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Will you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, and I'm talking once again about the situation of the Ministry of the Interior of Macedonia in 2001, that if a volunteer had engaged in the operation in Ljuboten without receiving a call-up notification to be a reservist prior to those events, he or they would have been there illegitimately and could only be regarded as volunteers but not as de jure members of the MOI. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order for me to answer, I actually have to know what exactly the status of volunteer of Ministry of Interior is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I will simply ask you this. In a situation where a person would volunteer to take part in a particular operation or in any other activities of the police, without a call-up notification to become a reservist, you would agree that any involvement in this particular activities would be illegitimate and that the individual in question could not be regarded as a de jure member of the MOI. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux has simply basically repeated his last question, and Mr. Bezruchenko has said you need to explain to me what the status of a volunteer of the Ministry of Interior is. Why are we going around in a circle again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm happy to reformulate, Your Honour, to expedite things if that assists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you agree that the procedure or the regular procedure for calling up of police reservists would entail, according to the procedure, a call-up notification. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there should be some document which would specify who is supposed to report where and in which situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you also aware of the fact there are other conditions set out in the laws applicable to the Ministry of the Interior for an individual to become formally or de jure a member of the police forces. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could perhaps refresh my memory, sir, and specify what specific conditions you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, for example, do you agree that there is a requirement of training to become a de jure member of the police. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting this is not a requirement set by the law, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the requirements of the law are a little bit broader than that. They actually stipulate specific educational parameters and conditions for personnel to be engaged in the role of police.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of the indications which -- or one of the -- yes, indication that a particular individual and one of the conditions set by the law to an individual becoming a reservists of the police would be the provision of an identification card of the Ministry of Interior. Is correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember seeing a document suggesting that reserve police personnel should have identification cards.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. Bezruchenko. I'd now like to turn to a different document that relates to information which I asked of you a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I could ask the registry to please bring up what is Rule 65 ter 1D724, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you recognise this document as a summary and analysis, this is title, prepared by you of the book by Mr. Ljube Boskoski "My Struggle for Macedonia"?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is a matter that I would like to clarify first with you, Mr. Bezruchenko. Clearly the first page contains a mistake, I believe, as to the date. It refers to the 24th of April of 2001, but then if you look in the next paragraph it refers to the 2001 and 2002 and to the fact that the book was published in 2004 in Skopje. And from the content of the summary, I do understand the book -- or the summary, I apologise, to have been done not on the 24th of April of 2001 but on the 24th of April of 2004. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, it could not really be done in one day. Yeah, it must have been 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I suppose that you recall preparing that particular summary for the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will also -- or I should put it that way, you will confirm that the summary and the analysis of the book of Mr. Boskoski which is in front of at this stage was prepared by you prior to the time when you became an expert for the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall making your particular -- or your personal, I should say, assessment and evaluation of the content of the book of Mr. Boskoski, the -- My Struggle for Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean, so what do you mean personal evaluation?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, there's a word missing from the transcript. I apologise, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you recall not only summarizing the book written by Mr. Boskoski but also include your personal analysis of the content of that book. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, basically it is not really analysis. This is rather a summary, and essentially it covered all the relevant chapters. Of course, it is not really a direct translation. Therefore, this is a very condensed summary of the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will just first draw your attention to this particular page. Do you agree that it refers to a summary and analysis, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry can please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that what appears on the screen here appears to be your summary of the first chapter of the book. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if one can turn to the second page of the document, please, or the third page, I apologise. This would be a summary of the second, third and you start with chapter 4. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chapter 4 is at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. But if one may turn now please to what is page 17 of the document, that would be 1D00-6427, please. And if I can ask to you look at the second half of this page, Mr. Bezruchenko, do you agree that there is a subsection called or entitled by you as "Analysis." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at the particular analysis which you made of the book of Mr. Boskoski. It says this: "The analysis of the book suggest a number of conclusion and investigative leads." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you would agree that this first sentence suggests that at least as far as the analysis is concerned, this was more than just military analysis. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this book is irrelevant for a military analysis of the conflict, and therefore, my analysis included certain matters related to the conflict as -- related to the conflict as reflected in this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that what they are characterised by you to be are investigative leads, is that correct, that's what you have named them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if one goes to the first paragraph of that analysis, it says this, that's what you wrote: "Boskoski's views were formed under the strong influence of radical Macedonian disguised as patriotism. He espouses strong nationalist idealogy." So just stopping there for a moment, Mr. Bezruchenko, do you suggest that this still falls within the realm of military analysis?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the ideological aspect of the conflict was not really my task, but if you take a look at the report in its entirety and especially the part of it which is devoted to paramilitary groups, you will note there that I also quote various sources which deal with the radical Macedonian groups and their ideology.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree here, sir, that you are dealing not with the ideology of the conflict -- I'm trying to find your exact term of the groups -- but what you suggest the views and political views of Mr. Boskoski's are. Do you agree with that.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not suggesting what Mr. Boskoski's views are, but I'm saying that they were formed apparently under the influence of radical Macedonian ideology.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you say in the next sentence is, "Boskoski's uncompromising support for the military option during the conflict as well as his obviously confrontational nature brought him into conflict with political opposition, Albanian parties, and international community." I hope you can agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this sentence and this view which you express about the nature of Mr. Boskoski, as you name it, falls well beyond the realm of military analysis. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer to your conjecture, sir, would be as follows. This book is a important source for understanding the accurate facts which occurred during the time of conflict in Macedonia. This particular sentence which you have just quoted in relation to support for military option during the conflict is certainly an important point which I derived from this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Therefore -- therefore, it is my position and my view that in fact this book is a primary source for military analysis and as such was analysed for featuring in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about the obviously confrontational nature of Mr. Boskoski, you claim he had? Did you see that that sort of analysis was relevant to what had been later requested of you as an expert?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this paragraph in its entirety is based on the analysis of the book, particularly one of the chapters, I think, in which he describes his relationship with various political parties and members of the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is that correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that in fact this particular summary and analysis of Mr. Boskoski's book was prepared by you prior to the time when you were asked to become the expert of the Office of the Prosecutor? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can look to the next paragraph in that document it says that "Boskoski's relationship with media and his statements suggest that he was conscientiously cultivating an image of a dedicated fighter for Macedonia, democratic brother Ljubo perhaps aspiring to become a national leader." Mr. Bezruchenko, do you agree that this particular statement or suggestion of yours again falls far beyond the realm of military expertise. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily, sir. This statement cannot really be regarded in isolation from the entire analysis of the book. It was the book which was the subject of the analysis. And this analysis is based on its entire contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask the registry now please to turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I will ask to you look at paragraph 3 of that document. I'll read it out to you. It says this: "Throughout the Albanian/Macedonian conflict, Boskoski displayed a strong 'hands-on approach' which was manifested in his activity to raise special police unit, frequent visits of the front-line police units, as well as his direct involvement and control of combat operations of these units." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's the same type of statement or findings which you later made in your report as an expert. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. What exactly do you mean the same type?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, is that correct that the suggestion that Mr. Boskoski was directly involved and control of combat operation of those units, and you are referring to special units, is to be found almost verbatim in your later report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact their entire analysis of this book does suggest that Mr. Boskoski indeed was very frequently seen with his troops on the ground and was obviously giving directions regarding the operations. Well, this book actually served as a basis for some of my assumptions and my analysis of the entire conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you go on to say this: "In the process, he was exposed to risk to his life several times. This kind of behaviour and style of leadership reflect the attitudes of a military commander who feels that he alone is in charge, assumes responsibility for his actions and personally leads his troops into action. Again, is it correct that this view which you had expressed to your colleagues at the time was again reiterated in your report where -- and in your evidence where you have sought to suggest that, in effect, the Ministry of Interior and the minister function, in effect, like a military body. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the analysis which is derived from this book. You can just read it and see for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 4 you said this: "Boskoski's admission that the operation in Ljuboten was a joint action of the Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Defence provides a valuable lead for development of the concept of joint criminal enterprise." Mr. Bezruchenko, would you agree that this statement lies far beyond the competencies and the mandate of a military analyst as you described at the beginning of your evidence. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain, sir. Well, I think as a military analyst, I was supposed to provide an appropriate analysis of the conflict in Macedonia as well as the developments in the village of Ljuboten as reflected in one of the sections of my report. As to the recommendations that I'm making at this point, these are essentially my ideas, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We adjourn now and resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could the registry please bring up, one again, Rule 65 ter 1D724, please. And if we can turn -- go back, please go back to page 18. That would be 1D00-6428. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I'll ask to you go back to the paragraph that we've left before the break. It's paragraph 4. And the next sentence after the one I had already left -- read to you reads as follows: "In the course of further investigation, the level of coordination between the Ministry of Defence and Ministry of Interior has to be thoroughly explored." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that this in effect are what can be characterised as investigative suggestions that you make to your colleagues. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily to my colleagues. In fact this whole document, this summary, and the analysis which accompanies it, in fact was my product which I was doing in the process of getting the understanding of the conflict as well as various aspects of what had happened in the village of Ljuboten. Well, whether it was intended for my colleagues, this is an entirely different matter. I think for most parts in this analysis I am providing certain information as well as leads for further analysis, which was entirely in my job description.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that this particular document was communicated or transmitted to your colleagues of the Office of the Prosecution who were involved in this investigation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the last sentence of that paragraph you say this: "During interviews of senior military and police suspects, this point should be in the focus of investigative effort. So again, would you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this is not military analysis but in effect an investigative suggestion that you make to your colleague. Do you agree with that -- colleagues?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mandate of the military analysts, sir, includes not necessarily in describing the conflicts or concentrating exclusively on military matters related to conflict situations but also analysis of the suspects and senior military and political figures which might feature in this or that investigation. So I don't really see any problem here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that when describing your mandate as a military analyst at the beginning of your evidence, you never suggested that this mandate would include the investigation or otherwise of the suspects and senior military and political figure which might -- figure -- I think it was "figure" you used in that or that investigation. Do you recall being asked to describe your duties as a military analyst?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall the fact that you never mentioned that particular aspect of your duties. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I didn't, but it does not necessarily mean that investigation should not be accompanied by military analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact you agree that - and we will come back to this over the course of this day or tomorrow - that you took an important part in the investigation of this case. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took part investigation of this case, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you took an important part, I'm putting it to you, in, for instance, obtaining documents, requesting documents, receiving documents, or taking part in interviews. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, for the time being, let's stay with the documents. We will come to those issues somewhat later. At paragraph 5 you made the following comment: "Boskoski admitted that he was in Ljuboten in the afternoon on 12 August on specific request of President Trajkovski and Prime Minister Georgievski. This admission presents a new and important angle of the investigation and possibly could provide exculpatory evidence." So do you agree, again, Mr. Bezruchenko, that what you're doing here is not military analysis. What you are doing is investigative work on behalf of the Office of the Prosecution. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, not necessarily, sir, because first of all this document was prepared before I started doing my report. And secondly, even while doing my report, one of the focuses of my report was the developments in the village of Ljuboten. And I don't think any responsible analyst would really drop such an important document as the book of memoirs by the former Minister of the Interior regarding the conflict in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But just a matter of timing here, Mr. Bezruchenko, it's -- you've explained or you've said on a few occasion that the reason for this was that part of your report had to do with the developments in the village of Ljuboten. But just to be clear on that point, in April of 2004 when you prepared that particular document, you had not started preparing your expert report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was working on the case in any case, yes, I was examining the documents, I was studying the conflict in Macedonia, I was doing my research in Internet and the other sources, so it was just a part of -- I was reading books, so it is just a part of these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But just to answer my question, Mr. Bezruchenko, at the time you agree that when you were doing that particular analysis of the document, you were not yet writing a report, an expert report that should be used in evidence in this case. Do you agree with that? And the indication that you have given that these particular aspects of the case or the material were relevant to the Ljuboten part of your report is simply not correct, since at the time you were not in the process of preparing this report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. Could you please repeat the last sentence again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll put it that way. You have explained on a number of occasion that the reason for the number of comments which you made in this document which is in front of you in relation in particular to Mr. Boskoski or otherwise who was in the village, was relevant to your effort as an expert to uncover what was happening in the village of Ljuboten. What I'm putting to you, sir, is, it simply cannot be the case it's at the time you were not yet working on an expert report on behalf of the Prosecution. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, an expert is somebody who knows more than a ordinary person about a certain specialized expertise or knowledge. My expertise and knowledge is military in specific relation to the former Yugoslavia, including Macedonia. I have been dealing with this issue for many, many years and saying that I was not analysing what had happened in Macedonia or Yugoslavia, for that matter, prior to compiling my report is simply not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if I understand your response to the question, is it correct that in fact at the time when you were preparing that report the comments, suggestions and otherwise contained in that documents were done not for the purpose of preparing your report at the time, but for the use of the Office of the Prosecution investigation team including yourself. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, this document was done for my own use, for my own exploration of possible inroads into this matter. This is exactly what I was supposed to do under the terms of my job description.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that it also contains several suggestions to your colleagues about further investigation or investigative efforts. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Analysis, rather, analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bezruchenko, I'm simply quoting from paragraph 4 of your own summary and analysis. It says: "In the course of further investigation," and the next sentence says "investigative effort." Do you agree that's what you told in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 5 you say the following. I will simply read the previous sentence again. It says: "This admission presents a new and important angle of the investigation and possibly could provide exculpatory evidence. A decision should be made if the role of Prime Minister Georgievski in the chain of command should be explored in the course of investigation. Do you recall making that comment?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just going back for a second to a proposition I had put to you a moment ago. It was at page 54, line 23. It starts at line 23. I read it out to you once again. It says this: "I'm putting it that you those concerns related in particular to concerns which you expressed to colleagues that in the absence of clear evidence that those you believed to have committed the crimes were members of the Ministry of Interior, you would be hard put to establish a line of command between Mr. Boskoski and those persons and you also expressed the view to your colleagues that as a result of that, you would encounter difficulties proving Mr. Boskoski's disciplinary duties in relation to these people." And then I asked you, "do you agree with that." And your answer was this: "Well, I have been having, well, my views on certain documents and certain aspects of the description of the conflict, but that does not necessarily mean that I actually expressed anything like this." And if I can now to turn to paragraph 6, Mr. Bezruchenko, of this summary and analysis of yours. You noted the following: "Boskoski also admitted that he signed the order about demobilisation of reservists in the area of Skopje on 29 June 2001. It has to be verified, if necessary, if reserve police personnel engaged for attack on Ljuboten received call-up notification and when. If they did not, police reservists engaged for attack on Ljuboten were there illegitimately and could be there only as volunteers." Do you recall saying that, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you go on to say: "They were probably hand picked by Tarculovski on Boskoski's orders. This may explain why former and serving individual Kometa members were engaged for attack on Ljuboten. To this date, the investigation did not reveal any contractual obligations between the Ministry of Interiors and Kometa. This informal relationship also could have implications for later investigations made by the Ministry of Interior..." and if we can turn the page "... this informal relationship also could have implication for later investigations made by the Ministry of Interior and disciplinary sanction which should have been applied to perpetrators." Do you recall now making those comments, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that again what you were expressing to your colleagues were matters of investigation that had to be verified with a view to build a case against Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, Mr. Mettraux, these were the analytical analysis, the analytical matters which have been derived from this book, and I think that my colleagues who are working on this case had the full right to be aware of what this book was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look at my question once again, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you agree that again you were expressing to your colleagues -- the matters which you were expressing to your colleagues were matters of investigation that had to be verified with a view to build a case against Mr. Boskoski. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation was going on, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And with that analysis, comments, and suggestion to your colleagues, you were in fact contributing to building up a case against Mr. Boskoski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the implication of your question Mr. Mettraux. If you're implying that it is not my job to provide any analysis or to an investigation team, this is simply a wrong assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I'm not trying to imply this. What I'm asking you is whether the nature of what you were doing, in particular in relation to those comments, was to make suggestions to your colleague as to how to make a case against Mr. Boskoski and matters which had to be verified with a view to do so. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also agree that at the time, as is clear from this paragraph, you were aware of at least possible or potential difficulties in establishing a relationship between Mr. Boskoski on the one hand, and members of this agency called Kometa. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of many other things, Mr. Mettraux, including various open options and scenarios of analysis. Well, therefore, it was basically my duty to read whatever documents come into my hands, including this particular book, and analyse it with the view of presenting my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But just sticking with the question for a moment. Do you agree that one of the concern which you expressed to your colleague and one of the matter which you suggested should be the subject of further investigation was the matter as to whether a relationship could be established between members of the Kometa agency and Mr. Boskoski. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- this issue, if you want to describe it this way, directly relates to the developments in Ljuboten in August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So the answer to the question would be yes. Is that correct, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since it was my task to describe the events in Ljuboten, to present a summary of those events in August 2001, I was supposed to explore all possible scenarios.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, again, Mr. Bezruchenko, you have indicated that this report was prepared prior to the time when you were tasked with preparing a report as an expert on behalf of the Prosecution which included a summary of those events in August of 2001. Are you in fact suggesting, Mr. Bezruchenko, now that you had started working on this report before that time?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid there is a contradiction, a contradiction in your statement, Mr. Mettraux. Would you please read it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, Mr. Bezruchenko, if there was a contradiction. You have indicated in answer to my question that, "Since it was my task to describe the events in Ljuboten to present a summary of those events in August 2001, I was supposed to explore all possible scenarios." Do you recall that, saying that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this answer that you provided was in response to a query on my part as to the nature of what you were doing, is that correct, at the time?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And my -- and also all documents which were available to me, including this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you see, Mr. Bezruchenko, at the time when you were preparing that document, you had not yet been tasked with the responsibility to prepare an expert report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But I don't see the point here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the point and I'm putting it to you is that well before the time when you were asked to become the so-called expert in this particular case, you had long started investigating the responsibility, in your view, of Mr. Boskoski. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really see any contradiction here again, because as I say, I have been dealing with the issues of armed conflict in the Balkans for many, many years, including this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But I'm going to come back to this issue at some stage but I'm going to put a proposition to you at this stage, Mr. Bezruchenko, and I will come back to this tomorrow. But do you agree that the reason why you were selected to be an expert by the Prosecution was not because of your expertise but because of the fact that your views were known to the Office of the Prosecutor and that they fit perfectly with the theory of the Prosecution case. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, going back to paragraph 6 of your statement or of your summary and analysis, do you agree also that another one of those concerns or matters which required further investigation on the part of the Office of the Prosecutor had to do with the fact that in the absence of a demonstration that these Kometa persons who you believed had been involved in those events had in fact become members of the Ministry of Interior de jure there could be serious issues pertaining to the duties or otherwise of Mr. Boskoski as regard matters of discipline. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. What I am saying here is that there possibly could be a link between these units and Mr. Boskoski and essentially that we needed more documents to explore this link.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that what you are saying also is that in the absence of such a link between Mr. Boskoski and these individuals, there would be no disciplinary duties on the part of Mr. Boskoski in relation to those persons. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the view that should have been confirmed by legal experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in particular, you have indicated and I will read out to you again from paragraph 6, and you say this: "It has to be verified if reserve police personnel engaged for attack on Ljuboten received call-up notification and when. If they do not, police reservists engaged for attack on Ljuboten were there illegitimately, and could be there only as volunteers." Do you recall saying this?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was my analysis, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact, you must be aware that your office, the Office of the Prosecutor, took a number of steps to verify the matter as you had suggested in your analysis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact what came back from those steps and verifications which were made by the Office of the Prosecutor, was exactly what you had feared in your -- or the concerns that you had expressed in your summary, namely that the person whom you believed might have been involved in those events were not de jure member of the MOI. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of this, I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D930, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you look at the first at the top of this document, Mr. Bezruchenko, you will see it's a record of suspect interview conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor, and the date is -- well, Mr. Raatikainen was not so sure whether it was the 29th or the 30th of June of 2004. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was only about a month after you had prepared your summary. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please. And if the registry could please scroll down to the bottom of the page. I'll ask you to look at the last question asked on that page by Matti Raatikainen to Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I see Mr. Saxon on his feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Saxon, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very sorry to interrupt. It's just that on the first page I saw a very familiar name, but this person's name has been the name of a witness who's testified in this case, but it is also the same name of someone else who has been mentioned in this case. And I'm just wondering if you could clarify who the person --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to you, Mr. Saxon, and perhaps, Your Honour, we can go for a second into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps with the assistance of the usher, the second microphone of Mr. Bezruchenko is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, if you can look at the bottom of the page, please. There's a question that is being raised by Mr. Matti Raatikainen with the interviewee or the witness, Mr. Jovanovski. And the question is this: "So you were all volunteers?" And the witness says: "I was a volunteer." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page, please, to the top of the page. Mr. Raatikainen then asked this: "I mean, you were not called in as a reservist?" And the witness says: "No, no." So you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that what was happening here, to the extent that you can agree with that, was that in fact the investigator, Mr. Raatikainen, was verifying what you had raised was a concern about the status of the people who you believed might have partaken in these events by verifying whether these peoples were there as reservists or had been called up as such or whether as volunteers. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm not trying to be difficult. Perhaps I was being difficult. It is simply that we haven't seen a passage here in the transcript with reference to the interviewee and his presence in Ljuboten, or if we have, I have completely missed it, and I think that needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've lost me, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
