utterances.text: Well, Mr. Raatikainen asked, "You were called up as a volunteer?" "I was a volunteer called in as a reservist," but there's been no connection made yet to the events in Ljuboten. That's what I'm simply stating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: He could have been called up on another day at another place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see that. And could I just mention, Mr. Mettraux, in your questioning, it is -- the way you framed your last question slid across what I thought was a line of logic that shouldn't be slid across. It's one thing whether a matter identified by this witness was the subject of questioning or inquiry by a investigator. It's another thing whether that was because it had been mentioned by this witness, and I think you were --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I stand corrected, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- into the cause, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, to take it one or two steps back, is that correct that at the time Mr. Zoran Jovanovski, Bucuk, was the owner of the security agency known as Kometa to which you referred in your summary.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this a question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see a question mark, so I'm just waiting for to you finish the sentence. Okay. I'm not sure if this was the case, but if he was subject of a interview, it might have been. He could have been in the past.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that at the time it was the belief of the Office of the Prosecutor that Mr. Zoran Jovanovski, aka Bucuk, was the owner of the company called Kometa. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen documents which suggest that Kometa members could have been involved in these developments and that they could not have been involved. So basically I was reading these documents and I was thinking about them, trying to make my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But just coming back to the issue of Mr. Zoran Jovanovski, do you agree, sir, that it is and was the position of the Office of the Prosecutor that Mr. Zoran Jovanovski, Bucuk, was in July and August of 2001, the owner of the company known as Kometa. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you sir, because I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We're going to move in a minute to a document which may assist you. But staying with this particular document for a moment, do you agree in any case Mr. Zoran Jovanovski, Bucuk, gave an indication to Mr. Raatikainen that he, for one, had been in the Cair police station on the 25th and 26th of July of 2001 as a volunteer. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I say, I was not really involved in this interview, and I didn't really pay any specific attention or I didn't really attribute a lots of significance to this specific interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can down a little bit on this document, there's a question asked by a man referred to as Gramsci where he says this: "Am I correct there were volunteers who were getting weapons and they were volunteers who were there to fight?" And the witness says: "There were a lot of people there. I saw a lot of people there, so I went there as -- as we -- and I asked them, Please give me a rifle, I want to protect my family." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the record, Your Honour, I believe that on the first page he mentions -- or on the second page he mentioned the 25th and 26th of July 2001 at the police station SOL, that is PSOLO, and not the Cair police. Well, Mr. Bezruchenko, in view of the fact that you are not very familiar with this document, I will move on to another one. Are you aware of the fact that the Prosecution wished to interview a number of individuals as part of its investigation and that for that purpose it directed a requested the government of Macedonia that list of person be relieved of their duty to keep confidentiality or state secrets. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a routine matter. The investigation division interviews various people, including the suspects.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that this particular request was made in relation in particular to Mr. Zoran Jovanovski, aka Bucuk? Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact I think there are perhaps more appropriate persons to answer this question, Mr. Mettraux. This question perhaps should be directed to those who was really working on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, at this stage I will ask you if you are aware that the Office of the Prosecutor made a specific request on 14th of January of 2000 -- well, let me ask you the other one first. Are you aware of the fact that the Office of the Prosecutor asked to -- asked the Ministry of Interior through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs that a number of individuals, including Mr. Zoran Jovanovski, Bucuk, and a man known as Goce Rarevski who had been employed by the agency, security agency, that they be relieved of their duty to keep state secret or official secret. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course these names are definitely familiar to me, especially the one of Bucuk, but saying whether I was specifically aware of all the paperwork, including that particular date, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D933. It has a ERN 1D00-7900.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness to switch on the second microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, will you able to -- it's been fixed already. Thank you. Mr. Bezruchenko, can you see in front of you a letter from the Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Foreign Affairs which is dated the 23rd of February of 2004. And it is directed to the office of the International Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia in Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, the second page, please. I apologise, if we can stay for a second on the first page first. I apologise to the registry. If you can look first at the first paragraph of that document, Mr. Bezruchenko, it say that at a session of the government of the Republic of Macedonia on the 26th of January of 2004, the government reviewed a request of the International Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia for interviewing individuals in the capacity of witnesses or suspect and adopted a conclusion by which it guarantees that the person that will be called as witnesses will not be prosecuted in the state for disclosing certain type of information marked with certain level of secrecy and confidentiality presented during their interviewing. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then in paragraph 2 follows another piece of information, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs says that,"Accordingly, we inform you that the Ministry of Interior affairs, adopted decisions for release of the obligation for keeping an official secret which they learned about during carrying out or in relation to the carrying out of the work and the assignments at the job position they were disposed to for person that were or still are employed at the Ministry of Interior Affairs or that were or still are members of the reserve police of the Ministry of Interior Affairs." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you can see there's a list of names, many of which I'm sure will be familiar to you, which starts on this page. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please. Do you agree that the lists of names continues up to number 23. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 23 -- at paragraph 3 it says this: "At the same time, we would like to inform you that the Ministry of Interior Affairs notified us that they could not prepare decisions concerning the obligation for keeping official secrets for the individuals Zoran Jovanovski and Goce Rarevski employed at Kometa security agency in Skopje, as they are not employed at the Ministry of Interior Affairs nor have they been engaged as members of the reserve police of the Ministry of Interior Affairs." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at the time when you prepared for your report, Mr. Bezruchenko, were you aware of this particular document and piece of information which was provided to you by the Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember seeing this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the witness can now be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D934, please. It is ERN 1D00-7942. Before we look at the document itself, Mr. Bezruchenko, I'll ask you whether you can recall that as part of the investigation conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor, a request was made by your office for the financial records of, among others, Mr. Johan Tarculovski and Mr. Zoran Jovanovski, aka Bucuk. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember seeing the previous document which you indicated, sir, but I don't think I'm in a position to provide you any details since I was not really working on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if we can look at this particular document, it is a so-called RFA, request for assistance from the Office of the Prosecutor. It is dated the 14th of January of 2005. And if you can turn your attention to paragraph 2 of the document, please. Do you agree that in this particular paragraph the assistance which the Prosecutor was seeking from the authorities was to obtain information about I believe two accounts which belonged to Mr. Tarculovski. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the way it seems.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the query was also about payments that were being made on to the -- these or that account. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, Mr. Mettraux, I don't quite understand why you are asking me this question. I was not working on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if we look then at paragraph 3 of the -- of this document, Mr. Bezruchenko, it reads like this: "Information regarding all payments from the accounts mentioned in paragraph 1 in July and August 2001 to Zoran Jovanovski, aka Bucuk, or to his company called Kometa." Do you agree that at least as far as this document is concerned, Mr. Bezruchenko, it was the view at the time that the company, Kometa, was in fact Mr. Jovanovski's company. Do you agree that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be so specific in this assertion, Mr. Mettraux. What I would say that apparently the investigation was opening -- I mean was exploring all possible scenarios and all possible lists. This is all what I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree perhaps that at least this letter from the Office of the Prosecutor refers to the Kometa as "his company;" do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would rather prefer if you probably could pose this question to the author of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that what is being sought effectively from the Macedonian authority in relation to Mr. Tarculovski and Mr. Jovanovski are information pertaining to payment to their accounts for the period July and August of 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This what it would seem to suggest, but if I may make a point again that perhaps somebody who was working on this document would be in a better position to give the precise details, because I'm afraid I could simply mislead you with my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, would you be willing to confirm on the face of this document that is what the Prosecution was seeking to obtain, and I'm reading from paragraph 1: "Information regarding all entries in July and August 2001 as regard the bank accounts of the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Finance of the Federal Republic of Macedonia," and then in paragraph 2 it relates to Mr. Tarculovski and in paragraph 3 to Mr. Jovanovski, Bucuk, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Mettraux, I'm afraid I'm not in a position to comment on this document since I was not really working on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can assist there. Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that the information that came back from this particular request that was made on behalf of your office was that Mr. Tarculovski had in fact received money on his account for July and August of 2001 as he was entitled as a official of the Ministry of Interior, but that Mr. Jovanovski, aka Bucuk, or his company had never received any salary or payment during that period from the Ministry of Interior. Are you aware of that piece of information?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the --?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not exploring this issue at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D931.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, the document which is about to appear, or has appeared now on your screen, provides information to the Office of the Prosecutor in response to the original request made by the Office of the Prosecutor. This letter refers to your request Mar/T07/MAC-0088, which is the document I've shown you a document ago. And if you look at the bottom of the page of that document first, you can see what the Macedonian authorities responded to the query made by your office in January of 2005 was the following. It's a letter from 7 February of 2005, and it is signed by the liaison officer of the Ministry of Interior, Mr. Besim Ramicevic and it is addressed to the office of the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia in Skopje. And the subject is submission of information and documentation pursuant to the request by the Office of the Prosecutor. And if you look at the bottom of that document, of that first page, it says this: "The Ministry of the Interior made payments to Johan Tarculovski on a salary basis for the period July-August 2001 during which he was listed as employee of the Ministry of Interior." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could please turn to the next page. And go to the top of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It also says this: "The Ministry of Interior did not make any payments to the Kometa personnel and property security agency and its owner, Zoran Jovanovski. The Ministry of Finance informed us that they have not made any payments to Tarculovski, Zoran Jovanovski, and the Kometa personnel and property security agency for the period July and August of 2001. During July and August 2001, the Ministry of the Interior made two salary payments on Johan Tarculovski's account." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, is that correct that this information which is contained in the document, perhaps not document itself but that the content of that document was brought to your attention by your colleagues? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, really. Well, now I have my doubts whether I have seen this document, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But leaving aside the document itself for a moment, Mr. Bezruchenko, do you agree that the information which you had suggested in your original analysis of Mr. Boskoski's book in relation to Kometa's people had in fact been verified by the Office of the Prosecutor and what I'm putting to you or what I'm asking of you, rather, is whether the information contained in the document as opposed to the document itself was known to you.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I don't quite understand. Which information do you mean and which document are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. I will clarify this, Mr. Bezruchenko. Were you aware of the information provided by Mr. -- or by the Macedonian authorities through Mr. Ramicevic that Mr. Zoran Jovanovski, Bucuk, and the Kometa personnel had never received salaries or money from the Ministry of Interior or the Ministry of Finance in relation to the period July and August of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Virtually the same answer was -- the same question was asked about a moment ago and the witness responded, "I'm not sure, really. Well, now have I my doubts whether I have seen this document, actually."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question was about the content. I believe what the witness said and the effort which was being made was not whether -- I think Mr. Bezruchenko has indicated that he was not sure whether he had seen the -- the actual document which is now in front of him. What is being -- what I'm trying to ascertain from Mr. Bezruchenko is whether he was aware of the information which is contained therein, namely the fact that no payments had been made to Mr. Jovanovski and the personnel from Kometa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now you have clarified that question, maybe we can get an answer to that one, which isn't the one you were trying to put.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you want me to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you'd better.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is late in the day, Mr. Bezruchenko, so I will put the question once again to you. Were you aware of the information which is contained in the document, namely the fact that no payment had been made to Mr. Jovanovski and the personnel from Kometa by the Ministry of Interior and the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is this correct -- or perhaps let me show you another document, Mr. Bezruchenko. This would be exhibit P232 [Realtime transcript read in error "P3232"]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It can't be what the transcript suggests exhibit P3232.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I have even managed to confuse the record assistant. It would be 232, P232.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps it should not be broadcasted, Your Honour. I'm being forewarned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, are you familiar with the particular document which you have in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. But looks like a receipt of some sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if we can go perhaps to the second page of this document, please. You will see on this page there is the name of a person. I'll let you have a look at the name. And if we can turn to the next page, please. Does that assist you in recognizing this particular document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember seeing some documents of this nature, various receipts for various weapons, obviously, but this particular one, no, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recognise perhaps this document as one of the exhibits used in this trial, which is, as you mentioned, the receipts given by Witness M-054. Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were many documents which I have seen during the varies stages of the trial. But again, I'm afraid you're asking the same question for the third time, sir. I'm not sure if I have seen this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you agree that this document and as you mentioned a number of other similar documents were -- or known to you and reviewed by you. Do you agree with this first proposal?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I remember seeing some of these kind of document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this particular document appears to be one of those records or a receipt, as you properly called it, for the delivery of facilities such as I believe in the page in front of you an AK-47 and ammunition. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Which facilities do you mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I was trying to find a proper word for -- to describe weapons, AK-47 and ammunition that goes with it. Do you agree that this receipt is in fact a receipt for such weapon and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: AK-47 and ammunition, sir, is certainly not a facility, if I may say so. But it appears to be a receipt for weapon and ammunition, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
